 Judgment

The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by her in the road traffic accident that was allegedly occurred on 27.11.2023.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:

sentences.text: On 27.11.2023 at about 4.50 p.m. the petitioner was boarding boarding the bus in its front door of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA.10.F.0204, while so boarding the driver of the said KSRTC bus was suddenly and negligently moved the bus, due to which the petitioner fell down from the door and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Government hospital,
Nanjanagudu, after first aid treatment injured was shifted to K.R. Hospital, Mysore wherein the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient and discharged with an advice of regular followup treatment and bed rest.
Further the petitioner was also shifted ti KIMS hospital, Bengaluru and took treatment as inpatient.
Petitioner has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy, aged about 36 years and was doing Coolie work and earning Rs.750/- to 800/- per day.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue with her work and lost her income.

The respondent is the owner and internal insurer of the bus is liable to pay compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-
with interest.
Hence the present petition.

3. After service of notice respondent appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by contending that, the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA.10.F.0204 was on its schedule trip from Nanjanagudu Srikanteswara temple to Mysore, when the said bus was stopped in order to take allow the passengers to board the bus slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules by the side of the road and even before parking the bus the passengers rushed towards the bus to board the bus and though the doors were closed the fighting was created amongst the passengers and as a result the two passengers sustained minor injuries.
The respondent specifically submitted that no accident was caused by the involvement of the either of the bus in question or by the driver of the said bus.

The petitioner sustained injuries while fighting with another lady passenger but in order to make an unlawful gain, the petitioner twisted the fact and projected as if the injuries were sustained by RTA by falsely implicating the bus with collusion with the police.
Further it has denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner and also the injuries sustained by her due to the accident, treatment taken and amount spent towards medical expenses.
Hence, the respondent prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court at the time of pronouncement of judgment :
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, She has sustained grievious injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-10-F-0204 by its driver, in RTA took place on 27.11.2023 at about 4.50 p.m on Chamarajanaga-Nanjanagudu main road near Srikantehswara Temple, Mudikatte?

Further the petitioner examined two witnesses as examined as PW.2 and 3 and through them Ex.P18 to 23 were got marked.

On the other hand the driver of the bus is examined as RW.1 by the respondent.
6.
Heard the arguments and perused the materials that are available on record.

The learned counsel for respondent has relied upon the following citation:
1. ILR 2009 KAR 3562 in between Veerappa and another V/s. Siddappa and another.
2. 2009 ACJ 292 in between Gurappa Vs. Goudappagouda and another.
3. (2009) 15 SCC 165 in between North West Karnataka Road Transport Corporation V/s. Gourabai and others.

That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed her affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of her case, she has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar along with sketch, seizure mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 8.
9.

On perusal of Ex.P1, FIR which is registered on the basis of the first information given by one Nanjundaiah D.N. who is the husband of petitioner by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA.10.F.0204.

The contents of Ex.P2 complaint and Ex.P1 FIR Rashmi B V vs K.S.R.T.C on 26 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180499209/
3 supports the contention of the petitioner about the rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA.10.F.0204 which is owned and insured by the respondent.
In continuation of Ex.P1 & 2, the police drawn spot mahazar and rough sketch which are marked as Ex.P3 & 4.
The Ex.P6 is the IMV report which says that no fresh visible damages were found on the offending bus at the time of IMV inspection.

10. The charge sheet as per Ex.P8 was filed against the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA.10.F.0204 wherein the IO opined that rash and negligent driving by the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA.10.F.0204 was the sole reason for the accident.
11. In this case the respondent has taken specific contention by denying any RTA and also involvement of the bus or driver in the alleged RTA.

It is the specific contention of the respondent is that the present petitioner and another lady passenger made galata/quarrel between themselves and thereby sustained injuries in their galata but later to make a unlawful gain they are projecting the said injuries as injuries of RTA even though there was no RTA as contended by the petitioner.
To prove the said contention the respondent examined the driver of bus as RW.1 and also relied on the Ex.P12 MLC document.

The driver of the bus who examine before this Tribunal filed evidence affidavit by denying the RTA and stated that though the doors were closed due to fighting between the petitioner and another lady passenger, the petitioner sustained injuries.

By keeping the said defence in background if we verify the Ex.P12 the out patient record of K.R. Hospital Mysore discloses that on 27.11.2023 at about 07.01 p.m. the petitioner was taken to the said hospital wherein it is written as the petitioner came to their hospital "A/H/O RTA near Nanjangudu temple".
12.
In the Ex.P12 initially it is written as 'Assault' and thereafter the said word 'Assault' was striking out and it is written as RTA near Nanjanagudu Temple.

By relying on the said correction in the first page of Ex.P12 out patient record of K.R. Hospital learned counsel for respondent argues that initially entries of the medical records as to be considered and also argued that the petitioner has not sustained any injury in RTA but the same is twisted as RTA even though the petitioner has sustained injuries in a quarrel with co-passenger.
In this regard the learned counsel for the respondent relied on the following judgments.
2009 ACJ 292 in between Gurappa Vs. Goudappagouda and another.
"Para No.8

The absence of any complaint being lodged at an earliest point of time and the specific mention being made before the doctor regarding cause of injuries showing that it occurred due to the deceased slipping from the steps and suffering head injuries makes the situation abundantly clear.

The version sought to be made out before the Tribunal stating that when Kasturi was travelling on the motor bike as a pillion rider, the motor bike fell into a ditch due to rash and negligent driving of the motor bike, is a clear case of improved version in order to fix the liability on the insurance company.
Learned Tribunal has rightly dismissed the claim petition.
No illegality or perversity can be found in the reasoning, and conclusion arrived at by the Tribunal.
Hence, this appeal fails and the same is dismissed".

sentences.text: "Para No.3 The effect of the evidence of the doctor and Exhibit R-1 does not appear to have been looked into by MACT and the High Court.

MACT did not place reliance on the document Ext. R-1 on the ground that the brother of the injured stated that he did not know what was written in the document and his signature was taken on one page.

This conclusion overlooks the fact that a doctor will not take a signature on a piece of paper mentioning something which is not correct".
No doubt that in the first page of K.R. Hospital outpatient record dated 27.11.2023 initially it is written as Assault and thereafter by striking out it is written as RTA.

Further on the very same document in the 2 nd page which is made on 27.11.2023 at about 7.10 p.m., it is written as follows:
" Patient was brought to TC causality A/H/O injury to both feet RTA (pedestrian V/s Bus) at around 5.00 p.m. on 27.11.2023 near Nanjangudu Bus stand".
Thereby in the same document on 27.11.2023 at about 7.10 p.m. itself the petitioner gave details of the accident to the doctor and she has furnish the proper details stating that she has sustained injuries by a bus in an RTA.
13.
By relying on the contents of said outpatient records of K.R. Hospital the details MLC was also written in the K.R. Hospital.
The document on which the respondent relied shows that the petitioner gave proper details of the accident to the hospital authorities.
14. Coming to the evidence of RW.1 who is the driver of the offending Bus who disputed the accident, as admitted by him the charge sheet is filed against him by the investigating officer.
Further as admitted by the RW.1 he has not challenged the said charge sheet.
No grounds are made out to disbelieve the contents of charge sheet.

The view taken by this Court that the police records are prima facie proof in support of the case of the petitioner, is supported by the decision rendered in Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held thus:
"12.

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid facts, the Tribunal should have considered both oral and documentary evidence referred to supra and appreciated the same in the proper perspective and recorded the finding on the contentious issue No. 1 & 2 in the affirmative.

But it has recorded the finding in the negative on the above issues by adverting to certain statements of evidence of AW-1 and referring to certain alleged discrepancies in the FIR without appreciating entire evidence of AW-1 and AW-2 on record properly and also not assigned valid reasons in not accepting their testimony.

The Tribunal should have taken into consideration the pleadings of the parties and legal evidence on record in its entirety and held that the accident took place on 19.07.1992, due to which Tikaram sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same and the case was registered by the Uniara Police Station under Sections 279 and Rashmi B V vs K.S.R.T.C on 26 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180499209/
5 304-A, IPC read with Sections 133 and 181 of the M.V. Act against the first and second respondents.

The registration of FIR and filing of the charge- sheet against respondent Nos.1 & 2 are not in dispute, therefore, the Tribunal should have no option but to accept the entire evidence on record and recorded the finding on the contentious issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the appellants''.

Hence, by relying on the said precedent and denial in respect of police documents marked at Ex.P1 to 8, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA.10.F.0204.
Merely because the driver disputes the accident, the contents of charge sheet cannot be rejected.
The MLC document of the K.R. Hospital which are made on 27.11.2023 at 7.10 p.m. in the second page it clearly shows that the petitioner sustained injuries by the bus in an RTA.
15. Admittedly, the petitioner got injuries while she was boarding to bus.

If the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA.10.F.0204 was not negligent and not moved his bus when the petitioner was still boarding the bus the said accident was not going to be caused and also the petitioner was not going to get injuries.
The case of the petitioner is support with the charge sheet which is filed by the investigating officer after detailed investigation.
Further the conductor of the said bus is nor examined by the respondent to show that the said bus was not caused any accident and it is not involved in the accident.

This shows that there is a negligence on the part of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA.10.F.0204 and no grounds are made out by the respondent to show the contributory negligence of the petitioner.
16.

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
18. As per well settled principle of law the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
In the absence of rebuttal evidence there are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner.

All the materials available on record leading to show that,
petitioner sustained injuries in the accident took place on 27.11.2023 which was caused by the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA.10.F.0204 which belongs to the respondent.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that she has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA.10.F.0204 belongs to respondent.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
(a) TOWARDS PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
The petitioner has relied upon Ex.P.7 - wound certificate, which make it crystal clear that PW-1 has sustained severe injuries which are simple as well as grievous in nature.
Petitioner has also produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P17.

On perusal of the same it reveals that the petitioner has taken treatment at KIMS hospital Bengaluru from 30.11.2023 to 05.12.2023 and has treated for Post traumatic fracture of left inferior pubic rami with undisplaced fracture of right foot 5th metatarsal and underwent conservative management with analgesics.

Hence keeping in mind the injuries mentioned in wound certificate and discharge summary, it can be said that the petitioner must have undergone some amount of physical pain and sufferings, for which, an amount of Rs.30,000/- can be held to be just and proper compensation under this head.
(b) TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has contended that she has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- for her treatment and has produced medical bills which are marked at Ex.P15 amounting to Rs.41,665/-.
Out of these bills the discharge summary marked at Ex.P9 and the bills produced at Ex.P15 Sl.No.10 to 13, 17 to 23 and 36, 38 and 41 to 44 are seriously disputed by the respondent.
The serial number of bills and the date of the bill and amount of the said bill are hereby quoted below in a table for better appreciation.

Coming to the discharge summary marked at Ex.P9, as per Ex.P9 discharge summary the petitioner admitted to KIMS Hospital on 13.09.2024 and discharged on 17.09.2024.
As per Ex.P9 the petitioner admitted to KIMS Hospital for the treatment of "fever, Chillness from 5 days, Multiple join pain from 5 days and right lower limb pain from 1 week".
As per Ex.P9, during the said period the petitioner diagnosed for Chikungunya fever, Type II diabetes Mellitus and Hypothyroidism.
Thereby the treatment taken under Ex.P9 are not related to the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident.
The Bills which are referred above in the table are also related and belongs to the period of 13.09.2024 to 17.09.2024.
As such these bills are not related to the accidental injuries hence it cannot be considered.
The other bills marked at Ex.P15 are supported with discharge summary of KIMS Hospital marked at Ex.P17.
Hence, the no grounds are made out to disbelieving this other bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitle by rounding off the same i.e., Rs.26,820/- under this head.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that she was doing Coolie work and earning Rs.750/- to Rs.800/- per day.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced any documents.
In the absence of evidence the notional income of the petitioner is taken at Rs.16,000/- as the accident is of the year 2023.

sentences.text: On perusal of the Ex.P17 it reveals that the petitioner has taken treatment at KIMS hospital Bengaluru from 30.11.2023 to 05.12.2023 i.e., for a period of 6 days.
Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered.
Hence, the 4 months of period is considered as healing period including 6 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,000 X 4 months = Rs.64,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by her the petitioner examined Dr. Mahesh D.V. as PW.3, through him clinical notes with calculation sheets and X-ray with radiological report are marked at Ex.P.20 to 23.

According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner has sustained tenderness over the left hip, swelling of right foot, cut lacerated wound 1cm and 0.5cm over the right foot, fracture of the left inferior pubic rami and right 5th metatarsal bone.
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.

Petitioner suffered total disability of 25.44%
to the left lower limb and 8.48% to whole body.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
No other expert evidence are adduced by the respondent to disprove the alleged disability stated by PW.3 doctor.
According to the petitioner she was doing coolie work and sustained grievous injuries.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on her occupation to some extent.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 6% to the whole body.
The petitioner has produced Aadhaar card and PAN card marked at Ex.P10 and P.11.
As per the Ex.P10 & 11 the date of birth of the petitioner is 06.06.1987.
The accident was occurred in the year 2023.
So, as on the date of the accident the petitioner was aged 36 years.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '15'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 15 X 6% =Rs. 1,72,800/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per Ex.P17 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 6 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P7 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period she spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained she is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 6 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the injuries as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.6,000/- in total.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:

sentences.text: The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by her, which might certainly have deprived her of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a. Towards pain and agony Rs. 30,000/- b.

Towards medical expenses Rs. 26,820/-
c.

Towards loss of income during Rs. 64,000/-
laid up period d.
Towards disability Rs. 1,72,800/- e.

Towards food, nourishment and Rs. 15,000/-
conveyance f.
Towards attendant charges Rs. 6,000/- g.
Towards loss of amenities Rs. 20,000/-
. Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent is the owner and there is a internal insurance to the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
21.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.3,34,620/- (Rupees three lakhs thirty four thousand six hundred twenty only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondent.
The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of awarded amount of petitioner, 50% shall be released to petitioner on proper identification and remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in her name in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.

Hence, by relying on the said precedent and denial in respect of police documents marked at Ex.P1 to 8, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA.10.F.0204.
Merely because the driver disputes the accident, the contents of charge sheet cannot be rejected.
Further the conductor of the said bus is nor examined by the respondent to show that the said bus was not caused any accident and it is not involved in the accident.
This shows that there is a negligence on the part of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA.10.F.0204 and no grounds are made out by the respondent to show the contributory negligence of the petitioner.
16.
In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.
17. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
18. As per well settled principle of law the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
In the absence of rebuttal evidence there are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner.
All the materials available on record leading to show that,
petitioner sustained injuries in the accident took place on 27.11.2023 which was caused by the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA.10.F.0204 which belongs to the respondent.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that she has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA.10.F.0204 belongs to respondent.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.

opennyai_summary.decision:
But by considering the nature of the injuries as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.6,000/- in total.
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by her, which might certainly have deprived her of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a. Towards pain and agony Rs. 30,000/- b.
Towards medical expenses Rs. 26,820/-
c.
Towards loss of income during Rs. 64,000/-
laid up period d.
Towards disability Rs. 1,72,800/- e.
Towards food, nourishment and Rs. 15,000/-
conveyance f.
Towards attendant charges Rs. 6,000/- g.
Towards loss of amenities Rs. 20,000/-
. Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent is the owner and there is a internal insurance to the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.
For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.3,34,620/- (Rupees three lakhs thirty four thousand six hundred twenty only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondent.
The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Out of awarded amount of petitioner, 50% shall be released to petitioner on proper identification and remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in her name in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
